concerns: Hypothesis/test description is truncated ('...flips them negative, meanin', '...logged ou'); the exact stress procedure is unspecified.
affected_files lists bot/intel/ and bot/ai_council/, but promotion-gate logic lives under bot/aegis/research/ (promote.py); bot/intel/ is a runtime-artifact directory, not a code-change target.

Unclear whether a sitting champion failing cost-stress would be demoted; intelligent_champion.json may only be written via the governed promotion scripts after all gates pass - any revalidation must route through that path, not a side channel.
Stress parameters (spread/slippage multipliers, pass/fail thresholds, minimum sample size) are undefined; post-hoc threshold selection would reintroduce the very cost-noise artifact being tested.
Reusing existing records (sealed_holdouts.jsonl, outcome logs) must avoid label leakage and must be registered in ExperimentRegistry like every experiment.
votes.reason: The core idea is sound and safety-aligned: cost-stress revalidation of promoted challengers directly enforces the existing 'outcomes must be net of spread/slippage' rule and can only tighten the gate, never loosen one. No MT5 execution, live-YAML, or DEMO-check surface is touched, so there is no safety violation. However, the proposal is materially incomplete (evidence and test fields are truncated mid-sentence) and the declared affected files do not match where gate logic lives, so it cannot be approved for test as specified.
